messages:
sara: FYI seeing a p99 jump for Hypha-v2 after today's tokenizer patch. Alert fired at ~09:10 UTC. p95 unchanged but p99 for long-context requests (>12k tokens) went from ~1.1s to ~4.8s and a few 503s. Sample request IDs: rq_9a3f, rq_9a41. Can we triage?

opsbot: Alert: latency.p99 > 3s (hypha-v2, region=us-west) triggered at 4076543205. Group: support.

leo: Can you paste a repro payload / curl and the exact model tag? Is this new traffic or synthetic tests?

sara: Model header: `x-redwood-model: hypha-v2@2026-03-17+tokpatch`. Affected: production traffic hitting long-context endpoints (customer A + some internal tests). Repro curl below: 

```
curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" \
  -H "x-redwood-model: hypha-v2@2026-03-17+tokpatch" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input": "<very long conversation with ~13k tokens>", "max_tokens": 256}'
```

Logs: `2026-03-17T09:10:12Z hypha-v2 rq_9a3f stage=tokenize duration=120ms path=/generate user=custA` then `stage=serve duration=4800ms` then `error=503` for one sample. Also seeing `kv_cache_hits=0` in traces for long requests that previously had >60% hit rates.

leo: kv_cache_hits 0 is interesting. Did tokenizer IDs change? If token IDs are remapped the KV key composition changes and we can lose cache. Any tokenizer commit/PR reference?

sara: Tokenizer change landed in release notes: `tok-patch-2026-03-17` — it switches subword split around emoji + CJK boundary and also renumbers some frequent subtokens. PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/hypha/+/tok-patch-2026-03-17 (internal).

mike: Likely culprit is token ID remap. When token IDs shift, KV cache keys that depend on token ids become incompatible and we see cache misses plus re-encoding overhead. For long-context, that turns a cached prefix into full compute which spikes p99. I pulled a flamegraph from a repro run: 

```
flame: serve_total 4800ms
  kv_lookup 40ms
  kv_fetch_remote 2400ms
  decode/encode 1200ms
  attention_kernels 1100ms
```

mike: Note `kv_fetch_remote` dominating — previously it was ~150ms because we were hitting local prefix cache. Now it's remote fetch for many shards. Also saw `kv_cache_hits: 3%` for rq_9a3f.

alyssa: OK mitigation suggestions: 
- short-term: route 100% of long-context production requests for affected customers to `hypha-v2-legacy-tokenizer` (old token ID mapping) for 2-4 hours while we patch.
- medium: add a compatibility layer that rewrites token IDs on KV keys for the new tokenizer mapping (requires coordinated rollout with runtime).
- immediate band-aid: enable aggressive prefix caching TTL and pin the prefix cache to the previous token-id namespace for known customer cohorts.

sara: Can we do the short-term routing rollback without full model rollback? I prefer routing to legacy-tokenizer variant so we don't lose other changes. Also want customer A notified.

mike: I can push routing change in the smart-router config: add policy `route: hypha-v2-legacy-tokenizer` for requests with header `x-customer-id:custA` and for paths with `context_len > 10000`. I'll start a canary to 10% then 100% if stable. ETA 30m for canary.

leo: I'll run reproducer against `hypha-v2-legacy-tokenizer` and compare p99 numbers. If we get restores to baseline we proceed with wider routing.

sara: Also seeing a small number of 401s in the same time window — probably unrelated but creating a separate ticket for auth noise.

alyssa: I'll draft a customer-facing note that says we detected a tokenizer compatibility issue affecting long-context latency, we routed traffic to a legacy tokenizer to mitigate, and we're working on a permanent fix. Will post in status.redwood.ai and ping account team.

mike: Canary rolled at 10% at 4076543700. Initial results: p99 for canary requests ~1.2s, kv_cache_hits restored to ~62%. No increase in errors. Moving to 100% canary at 4076544000.

opsbot: Deploybot: smart-router config update `route-hypha-legacy` succeeded (deploy id dpl_7721) at 4076543998.

sara: After routing change, global p99 for hypha-v2 long-context dropped back to ~1.3s. Customer A confirmed lower latency in their integration tests.

jen: Good triage. Action items: 
- mike: implement compatibility rewrite for KV keys (owner, ETA 5d)
- eng-ml: add tokenizer mapping doc and auto-compat shim (owner leo/eng-ml, ETA 7d)
- support/ops: customer comms posted (alyssa, done)
- infra: add a preflight test to detect token-id remaps on onboarding (owner infra team, create ticket)

sara: Closing thread for immediate mitigation. Will reopen if we see reappearance after compatibility patch. Thanks all :thumbsup:

jen: Marking incident resolved for the routing mitigation, follow-ups tracked in ENG-2026-319.
